title: Labor & Delivery Language Access: A Workflow Guide for Maternity Teams
summary: Build an L&D language access workflow for triage, bedside care, anesthesia, postpartum teaching, and discharge.
body_markdown:
###


Interpretation should be available throughout triage, labor, pain assessment, anesthesia, procedures, changes in the birth plan, postpartum teaching, newborn care, and discharge. The exact modality can vary by patient preference, organizational policy, and the clinical situation.


###


Labor involves frequent, unscheduled communication and can change quickly. If interpretation takes too long to access, staff may be more likely to rely on workarounds for short but clinically important conversations.


###


Yes. With appropriate clinical controls, AI medical interpretation can be a first-line option for routine and complex communication. Human interpreters remain complementary according to patient preference, organizational policy, and encounter needs.


###


Make interpretation immediately available, discuss common anesthesia options before urgency develops when possible, and give patients enough time to ask questions. Interpreter access should be part of the anesthesia workflow instead of being arranged only after a decision becomes urgent.


###


Track time to active interpretation, use by communication type, staff workarounds, language-related safety events, use of translated postpartum materials, and patient understanding of discharge instructions and warning signs.
